newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya reshuffle brings back controversial Moi aide.
newsitem.headline: Kenya reshuffle brings back controversial Moi aide.

text.p: Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi announced a reshuffle on Wednesday that brought controversial former aide Nicholas Biwott back into the cabinet, five years after he had been dropped amid corruption charges.
Moi, in power since 1978, said in remarks relayed by state radio that the cabinet changes were motivated by the need for effective management in the east African nation.
Biwott, a close aide of Moi from his minority Kalenjin tribe, was named minister in the presidency, a powerful portfolio.
Biwott was dismissed in November 1991 after allegations of corruption and was also a suspect in the inquiry into the 1990 murder of popular former foreign minister, Robert Ouko.
Political analysts in Nairobi said Biwott's comeback was likely to upset western donors who underwrite lifeblood annual aid to the east African nation.
"This is a direct slap in the face of donors. It is simply unbelievable," said one western ambassador.
The radio statement announced the removal of Kipkalia Kones, a fellow Kalenjin, who had been minister in his office.

Biwott's position as industry minister in 1991 became untenable after British detective John Troon told a judicial inquiry into the Ouko murder that Biwott and late former security chief Hezekiah Oyugi were prime suspects.

Troon told the inquiry he believed Ouko was killed because of his opposition to corruption among his colleagues and because of disagreements with Biwott which surfaced during a trip to Washington in January 1990.
Ouko's charred and mutilated body was found in February 1990 in a bush near his Kisumu home, a few days after he asked for an inquiry into high-level government corruption.
Biwott, alleged by financial experts to have amassed a huge fortune, was a personal assistant and business manager to Moi when he was vice-president between 1969 and 1978.

Biwott quickly rose to prominence after Moi became president in 1978 on the death of Kenya's founding father Jomo Kenyatta. He was one of the first beneficiaries of Moi's efforts to consolidate power by replacing figures of the 1960s with political novices loyal to him.
Biwott's parliamentary colleagues have accused him of a patronising attitude, arrogance and an abrasive style.
Moi, saying he made the changes to encourage effective management in government, appealed to the new leaders to keep the interests of the country above their own personal interests.
"Leaders come and go. I call upon those responsible for conducting government business at all levels to be patriotic and commit themselves to serving Kenya," Moi said.
Moi demoted local government minister William ole Ntimama to the less important portfolio of national heritage, swapping positions with Francis Lotodo.
Simeon Nyachae, minister in the highly important agriculture portfolio was transferred to land reclamation, regional and water development.
Nyachae's job was taken by Darius Mbela, who moved from the ministry of tourism. Potters Momanyi was named as the new minister of tourism.
Health minister Joshua Angatia was moved to the commerce portfolio while General Jackson Mulinge was transferred from lands and settlement to the health ministry.
Former Commerce Minister Kirugi M'mukindia was named new energy minister, taking over from Noah Katana Ngala who moved to lands and settlement.
Kenya holds parliamentary and presidential elections this year.
